text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to read, not to add new features. For example, you might break a long, complicated function into smaller, simpler ones, or rename variables so they clearly describe their purpose. By doing this, you reduce what developers call "technical debt"—the extra cost of dealing with messy code later. Regular refactoring keeps the codebase healthy, saves time in the long run, and makes it much easier for new team members to understand and work with the project.
